title: What is known about 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, but the run is now understood up to its rebuilds. Between rebuilds the machine is a binary counter that applies one fixed operation to a list of blocks once per tick, and the list is the binary expansion of the time it has left (checked against the machine, not proved). Rebuilds are still simulated cell by cell. With this the run passes 243 rebuilds, more than 1010,642 steps, without a halt (before: three rebuilds, 3·1010 steps).

It can halt from tapes of its own shape. A single block of 3k cells that meets the counter exactly at the start of a round halts (k = 3 to 9, direct simulation). Whether the run from blank tape ever produces such a coincidence is the open question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 189 cells have been visited and 86 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in C on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps; three rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation for 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps. At the moments the head is in C on the first 0 right of everything written the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s; the last block grows by 4 per round; in walking phases the rounds satisfy T′ = 2T + 4 exactly. Rebuilds of the list at steps 72,083, 11,004,261 and 22,558,329,283 (the table).

claims.title: Between rebuilds: a binary counter that applies one list operation per tick
claims.text: At the moments the head is in C on a 0 just right of a 1, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (the interior), a last block l, and to the right of the head a zone of single 1s. Call it regular if the first block is a multiple of 3, the other interior blocks are 2 mod 3, l is 1 mod 4, and the gaps of the zone are 0 mod 4 (the first, counted from the head) and 3 mod 4 (the others). From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) a regular configuration changes in two independent ways. The interior takes one step W: (..., x, 3a + 2) becomes (..., x + 3, 2, ..., 2) with a blocks of 2. The last block and the zone are a binary counter: with segments s<sub>1</sub> = g<sub>1</sub>, s<sub>i</sub> = g<sub>i</sub> + 1, a last block l ≥ 5 becomes a new first segment l − 1 and l = 1; with l = 1 the n leading segments equal to 4 are removed, the next segment loses 4 cells (blank tape supplies them if there is none) and l = 4n + 5. So l plus the segments is 4m + 1 for 2<sup>m</sup> sub-rounds (one round, what earlier notes called the fast counter), then m grows by 1. Checked against the machine one sub-round at a time: of the 300,000 sub-rounds after step 2,918 (12.6 million steps) the 299,954 regular ones all follow this; the other 46 are the transients of the first two rebuilds. Observed and checked, not proved.

claims.title: The list is the binary expansion of the time it has left
claims.text: With digits ai = (bi − 2)/3, W removes the last digit a, adds 1 to the digit before it and appends a zeros; the sum of all digits plus their number never changes. A tail (..., q, a) becomes (..., q + a + 1) after exactly 2a steps, so an interior with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T = Σi 2ai + ... + ak + k − i steps of W: the positions of the 1s in the binary expansion of T are the partial sums of the list read from the right. (This is arithmetic on the rule W, not on the machine.) Checked on the machine: the model predicts single blocks at sub-rounds 1,616 and 261,907 of that run and both are there; W steps and counter steps taken many at once agree with the machine in 28 test jumps; and after the third rebuild the lists at seven ends of rounds, up to step 2.8·1010, are those of a direct run of the machine (3 2^25 14 2 8 2 14 | 85 at step 22,558,329,286, ..., 3 2^12 20 2^6 14 2 8 2 14 | 109 at step 28,107,393,382).

claims.title: Tapes of the same shape that halt
claims.text: A rebuild starts when the interior is a single block. The tape 1<sup>3k</sup> 0 1<sup>4k−3</sup> with the head in C on the 0 right of it, a single block of 3k cells meeting the counter exactly at the start of round k − 1, halts for every k from 3 to 9 (after 311, 659, 1,343, 2,699, 5,399, 10,787 and 21,551 steps; direct simulation). So no property of the shape alone can show that the machine never halts: it depends on which single blocks and counter values the run from blank tape produces.

claims.title: 243 rebuilds without a halt
claims.text: A run that takes the regular sub-rounds by arithmetic (any number at once, with the two rules above) and gives everything else to the machine itself, cell by cell: the transient after each single block, and the sub-rounds where the counter reaches an irregular gap of the zone. It passes 243 rebuilds; by then the counter has made more than 2<sup>35,353</sup> sub-rounds, so the machine more than 10<sup>10,642</sup> steps, and the single block has 106,062 cells. A halt could only be found by the direct part and none was. The arithmetic part rests on the two rules above for all sizes, which are checked, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Between rebuilds the machine cannot halt if the model is right; a rebuild's transient can (tapes of the same shape do). What the transient does to the block and the counter has no rule yet, so the question is whether the single blocks and counter values of this run ever meet in a halting way. The halting family above needs the single block to arrive exactly when a round of the counter starts, a coincidence of two binary numbers that the run has avoided so far.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Between its rebuilds this machine is a binary counter that applies one small operation to a list of blocks at every tick, and the list is, read in binary, the time left until the next rebuild. This page runs the machine, lets you step the list and the counter, and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt, more than 10<sup>10,642</sup> steps (model checked, not proved).
The model against the machine, one sub-round at a time.
Tapes of the same shape that halt.
Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.

sections.heading: A binary counter that rewrites a list
html: Stop the machine each time the head is in state C on a 0 just right of a 1. The tape is then a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, a last block, and right of the head a zone of single 1s. From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) two things happen, and they do not influence each other.

The list takes one step. Its last block, of 3a + 2 cells, gives 3 cells to the block on its left and falls apart into a blocks of 2: x, 3a+2 becomes x+3, 2, ..., 2. Counting a block of 3a + 2 as the digit a: the last digit a is removed, the digit before it grows by 1, and a zeros are appended.

The counter ticks. The last block and the zone hold a binary counter. A round is 2m sub-rounds in which they fill 4m + 1 cells; then the last block is 4m + 5 cells and round m + 1 starts. This is why each round takes twice as long as the one before.

The list gets shorter in the end, and how long that takes can be read off it: a list with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T steps, where T has a binary 1 at the positions ak, ak + ak−1 + 1, ak + ak−1 + ak−2 + 2, and so on. The list is the time it has left, written in binary. Try it:

The start values are the tape at step 2,918 from blank tape (last block 9, so round 2). All of this was read off the run and then checked against the machine: 299,954 regular sub-rounds one by one, jumps of many sub-rounds, and the lists at seven round ends up to step 2.8·1010. It is not proved.

Rebuilds. When a single block is left, the sub-rounds are irregular for a while: the block is cut into 3 2 2 2 ..., cells of the last block and the zone move into the list, and then the regular life starts again with a longer list. No rule is known for this part; the long run simulates it cell by cell. The first rebuilds:

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1. In a regular sub-round that does not happen (in the model). In the irregular stretch after a single block it can: the tape 1^(3k) 0 1^(4k−3) C>0, a single block of 3k cells arriving exactly when round k − 1 of the counter starts, halts for k = 3, ..., 9 (311, 659, 1,343, ... steps; each about twice the one before).

So the question is one about two binary numbers: the time T the list needs, which is written in the list itself, and the state of the counter. The run from blank tape has passed 243 rebuilds, more than 1010,642 steps, without a halt. Nothing proved says it stays that way, and the irregular stretches have no rule yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).
After 109 steps the tape spans 189 cells (10 left of the start, 174 right), with a density of 1s of 0.455.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

family: two-level block counter (fast tail, walker in a list of 2s, rebuilds)
summary: Binary counter applying one list operation W per tick; the block list is the binary expansion of the time to the next rebuild (checked, not proved); rebuild transients simulated directly; no halt in 243 rebuilds (more than 10^10,642 steps); tapes of the same shape halt; open.
